statements.quote: Carlene and I will also be presenting with friends and co-authors at the AACAP Conference in 2 weeks here in NYC!

statements.note: Own-activity announcement; low forecast value. Coder may mark CONTROL.

statements.quote: Will Clubhouse pick up our pilot? We’ll let you know as soon as we hear!
statements.context: The Frontier Psychiatrists Daily pilot episode (with guest Fredrick Brennan) was submitted to Clubhouse's Creator First program; the decision is pending and the author commits to report it. No directional call is made.
statements.note: Borderline: a question plus a commitment about a pending Clubhouse decision on the pilot; no stated expectation either way.

statements.quote: Join us this Thursday, May 20th from 12-5PM EST for Mental Health Action Day.
statements.context: Invitation to the newsletter's participation in Mental Health Action Day on Thursday May 20, 2021, 12-5PM EST (post dated 2021-05-19).
statements.note: Invitation / event announcement for the newsletter's own programming; low forecast value.

statements.quote: We were thrilled to see that Brandon Batstone and his show about the healing potential of psychedelics joined us, and is another important step in psychedelic medicine becoming more mainstream.
statements.context: In the post announcing selection to Clubhouse's first Creator First accelerator class, the author frames a psychedelics show joining the class as a step in psychedelic medicine becoming more mainstream. Implicit trend claim that mainstreaming of psychedelic medicine continues.
statements.note: Borderline: trend claim ('becoming more mainstream') with an implicit forward reading; no date or mechanism.

statements.quote: This summer, The Frontier Psychiatrists, Owen Muir, M.D. and Carlene Macmillan, M.D. will be rolling out engaging programming, with special guest interviews and talks on mental health debates, advances and controversies.
statements.context: Newsletter and Clubhouse programming plan for summer 2021: guest interviews, talks, AMAs on PTSD, personality disorders and depression, and collaborations with other Clubhouse creators. Setup: 'our Clubhouse conversations are expanding by the day'.
statements.note: Own-newsletter programming plan; coder may mark CONTROL.

statements.quote: Our Substack page will be the home base for all of this — with your support, we will continue dedicating more and more time and resources to creating this new culture of important, fun and exceptional mental health programming.
statements.context: The newsletter's Substack is to be the hub for the Clubhouse programming; conditional on reader (subscriber) support, the authors say they will keep increasing time and resources for mental health programming.
statements.note: Own-newsletter plan, conditional on reader support ('with your support'); compound (home base + more resources).

statements.quote: Next up…the iRig 2 and external audio equipment.
statements.context: End of part one of a how-to on getting external microphone audio into Clubhouse on an iPhone via the iRig MicCast2; the author announces a next installment on the iRig 2 and external audio equipment.
statements.note: Trivial: announces the next how-to post. Logged for recall only.

statements.quote: While the above is still quite a ways away from prime time for humans
statements.context: CTMSS 2021 recap. After Harold Sackeim's talk on a 2017 optogenetics study that turned 'loser' mice into 'winners' and the idea of cosmetic brain stimulation to dial up grit / 'learned resilience', the author judges that such human use is far off.
statements.confidence_phrase: still quite a ways away from prime time
statements.note: Horizon-only call: cosmetic brain stimulation for grit in humans is not near. Author also calls the idea 'both frightening and exhilarating'.

statements.quote: Dr.Sackeim was pretty confident that within a few years many of us psychiatrists in the room would be directly administering drugs locally in the brain.
statements.context: Harold Sackeim's prediction at the Clinical TMS Society 9th annual meeting (June 2021): within a few years psychiatrists will deliver drugs directly into the brain. He cited Cerebral Therapeutics (intracerebroventricular delivery; studies showing 77% seizure reduction with divalproex in temporal lobe epilepsy) and imagined clozaril delivered to the brain in schizophrenia. The author reports it and says 'Keep an eye on this company to see if his predictions come true!'.
statements.note: Third-party forecast (Sackeim). Author reports it without adopting it; stance is 'keep an eye on this company'.

statements.quote: Trials underway with VNS need to be several years long because results take time to accrue.
statements.context: Vagal nerve stimulation for treatment-resistant depression: works for a minority, but with dramatic and durable results for them. The author says ongoing VNS trials must run several years, which implies readouts are years away.
statements.note: Borderline: descriptive claim about trial duration; implies VNS depression trial results are years away.

statements.quote: As more and more psychiatrists start to incorporate interventional procedures like TMS and psychedelic medicine like Esketamine into their repertoire, device manufacturer registries and forward thinking mental health electronic medical record startups need to be on our radar.
statements.context: Presupposed trend: growing adoption by psychiatrists of interventional procedures (TMS) and psychedelic medicine (esketamine), which makes device outcome registries (Neurostar, Brainsway) and mental-health EMR startups (Osmind, Maya Health) important. The author has joined Osmind's Clinical Advisory Board.
statements.note: Trend presupposed in an 'as more and more...' clause; the 'need to be on our radar' part is normative. Author has an Osmind advisory role (possible CONTROL link).

statements.quote: Given the favorable side effect profile of TMS and concern around the systemic impact of some psychiatric medications, it offers great promise for this population.
statements.context: TMS for perinatal mood and anxiety disorders. CTMSS's affinity group launched a TMS Perinatal Registry; the author's practice has a perinatal team led by Dr. Amanda Tinkelman; a poster reported a 4-patient case series in pregnancy. The author expects TMS to become useful for this population while saying the field must still determine its place.
statements.note: Borderline: 'offers great promise' is an expectation, not a dated call.

statements.quote: It is possible that a different protocol could work for PTSD in conjunction with SDI, such as a protocol targeting the dorsolateral prefrontal cortex, could have more promising results but further research is clearly needed.
statements.context: After Brainsway medical director Aron Tendler presented a failed deep TMS trial for PTSD (sham beat active; the medial prefrontal cortex target seemed to interfere with script-driven imagery exposure), the author speculates that a DLPFC-targeting protocol combined with SDI could succeed.
statements.note: Hedged clinical hypothesis; compound with 'further research is clearly needed'.

statements.quote: There was a lot more and paid subscribers will have access to some audio excerpts from our recent pop-up Clubhouse room were we discussed the conference and took general audience questions about TMS. Look out for that post soon as well as others about mental health, social audio (including some technical audio guides thanks to Owen) and more.
statements.context: Newsletter content plan at the end of the CTMSS recap: paid-subscriber audio excerpts from a Clubhouse room about the conference, plus more posts on mental health and social audio, including technical audio guides by Owen.
statements.note: Own-newsletter content plan; low forecast value. 'were we discussed' is the original text.

statements.context: Show schedule: second episode of the Creator First show on the Friday after the post (post dated 2021-06-20, so June 25, 2021) at 1pm EDT, called the new regular timeslot.
statements.note: Event announcement for own show; low forecast value.

statements.note: Event announcement plus an expectation ('should be a rich discussion'). Two sentences joined with ' ... '.

statements.quote: Tomorrow, we will be focusing on gamification on social audio, with a panel of diverse views that include behavioral scientist Matt Wallaert
statements.context: Creator First show episode on gamification in social audio scheduled for the day after the post (post dated 2021-06-24; the show's regular slot is 1pm EDT Fridays). Panel: Matt Wallaert, Anna Lembke, Bethania Bacigalupe ('The Pricing Nerd'), Brian Fanzo, Julia Koerwer.
statements.note: Event announcement for own show; low forecast value.

statements.quote: our Sunday night AMA Frontier Psychiatrist show will be continuing and include special guests from mental health, the music industry, athletes and more.
statements.context: Programming plan: the Sunday-night AMA show on Clubhouse continues, with guests from mental health, music and sports. The post also says podcast excerpts of shows are being published for paid subscribers.
statements.note: Own-show programming plan; low forecast value.

statements.quote: While we wait for the blizzard of content coming from our Clubhouse activities, a blast from the past-cast.
statements.context: Podcast blurb republishing Owen's first podcast episode (Rudin Fellowship project at NYU School of Medicine); the author says a large volume of content from the Clubhouse shows is coming.
statements.note: Trivial: promise of upcoming content volume. Logged for recall only.

statements.quote: LinkedIn, Discord, Reddit and others are following suit in diving into the live social audio space.
statements.context: Opening of the gamification essay: Spotify launched Greenroom on June 16, 2021 after Twitter Spaces, then Facebook launched Live Audio Rooms; the author says LinkedIn, Discord, Reddit and others are entering live social audio too.
statements.note: Borderline: present progressive ('are following suit') read as near-future market entry by these companies.

statements.quote: If we apply this principle to the social audio world, it is possible that the addition of gems, stars or other outward reward systems could make people less likely to want to participate on a platform despite rich conversations happening on them.
statements.context: Applying panelist Matt Wallaert's point that extrinsic rewards degrade intrinsic motivation: gamification via Greenroom gems (Spotify) and Facebook stars could reduce participation on social audio platforms. Followed by: if extrinsic rewards become the driving force, 'we are in trouble'.
statements.note: Hedged behavioral forecast about gamified social audio platforms. Post voice appears to be co-author Carlene MacMillan's.

statements.quote: The CTO of the sports-focused Locker Room, which is what Greenroom was called before being acquired by Spotify, has discussed with the Greenroom community that they are actively looking to refine how the gems operate.
statements.context: Reported via panelist Christian Bourdeau: Greenroom (Spotify) leadership intends to change how gems work. Greenroom had already moved gem-giving from a 5-minute to a 30-minute interval.
statements.note: Reported third-party intention (Greenroom CTO, via a panelist); not the author's own call.

statements.quote: This is the absolute worst combination for performance enhancement and would be expected to result in high initial engagement but then significant churn of users growing bored as the novelty wears off.
statements.context: Greenroom gems (Spotify) as designed in July 2021: lowest possible standard (no real value) with highest confidence of obtaining them (press a button at a fixed interval), framed via Claude Steele's expectation/performance study raised by Matt Wallaert. The author predicts high initial engagement then significant user churn, and notes their own Greenroom use already dropped off.
statements.note: Main forecast of the post: Greenroom gem gamification leads to user churn. Post voice appears to be co-author Carlene MacMillan's.

statements.quote: which is perhaps in part why there is a massive interest in Avatar oriented NFT projects like Bored Ape Yacht Club and will be the subject of a future Frontier Psychiatrists Clubhouse show on Aug 13th
statements.context: Aside during Anna Lembke's remarks about accumulating digital objects: the newsletter announces a Clubhouse show on avatar NFT projects (Bored Ape Yacht Club) on Aug 13, 2021.
statements.note: Event announcement for own show; low forecast value.

statements.quote: She suggested that based on what we know about operant conditioning the use of variable unpredictable intervals regarding how often gems can be awarded would result in the most sticky use of them.
statements.context: Panelist Rowshanak Hashemlyoon (behavioral neuroscientist) predicts that variable, unpredictable gem-award intervals would make gems stickiest for users. The author calls this 'the most intriguing possibility', compares it to Clubhouse's early invite system, and adds that gambling and video game industries know this principle and 'it stands to reason' that anyone gamifying a platform should consider it.
statements.note: Conditional design forecast originating with panelist Hashemlyoon; author endorses the principle ('most intriguing possibility', 'it stands to reason'). own_claim is debatable.

statements.quote: Therefore, online social media platforms from TikTok to YouTube to Clubhouse, have an increasingly large role to play in educating people about mental illness.
statements.context: Essay on faked mental disorders (DID, Tourette's, ADHD, autism) trending on TikTok. Because professional assessments are costly and waitlists long, the author says social platforms will increasingly educate the public about mental illness.
statements.note: Borderline trend claim ('increasingly large role'). Post voice appears to be co-author Carlene MacMillan's (McLean Hospital attending).

statements.quote: If we as licensed professionals don’t join in these conversations, we run the risk of influencers with zero mental health or medical training having the loudest voice and glamorizing disorders in ways that invalidate the experiences of those who actually have them.
statements.context: Conditional forecast: if licensed clinicians stay off TikTok, YouTube and Clubhouse, untrained mental health influencers will dominate and glamorize disorders such as DID and Tourette's.
statements.note: Conditional; consequence framed as a risk, not a definite outcome.
